data.description:
Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Options-parity golden snapshot for shipped story-line content

## Summary

Pin the behaviour this refactor must not change, before any deletion happens.
Record the compiled option list of every shipped story-line card in a committed
golden fixture and add a unit test that recompiles the content and compares. The
test is green today and must stay green after every removal phase, so any
compilation drift surfaces immediately instead of at the end of the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A committed fixture `tests/fixtures/story-line/options-parity.json` records, per shipped card id: card name, storyline id, and the ordered compiled options (label, ordered successor ids, `effectPolicy`).
- The fixture covers the Gym content (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` compiled with `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER`) and the Main Street reference-pack copy (`tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` compiled with a minimal options-only adapter declared in the test).
- A unit test recompiles both files through the public content API (`cardsFromCsv` then `compileContentOptions`) and deep-equals the fixture, so drift fails with a readable diff.
- Explicit assertions (on top of the deep-equal) cover at least one multi-option card, one terminal option (`successorIds: []`) and one plain incident with an empty option list, so the intent of the snapshot is legible without reading the fixture.
- The test passes against the current pre-refactor code: the baseline is captured from real behaviour, not hand-written.
- The test asserts shipped-content behaviour (CSV in, compiled options out); it is not a source-code grep over `src/`.

## Key Files

- `tests/story-line/options-parity.test.ts` — new golden-parity test (unit profile).
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/options-parity.json` — new committed golden fixture.
- `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` — the shipped Gym content the snapshot pins.
- `tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` — the shipped Main Street reference copy the snapshot pins.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — the projection/compilation entry points the test drives.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the test so it builds the snapshot from the shipped CSVs and prints the computed JSON when it mismatches.
2. Run it once, review the captured snapshot for plausibility (labels and orders must match the `options` encodings in both CSVs), and commit it as the golden.
3. Add the three representative assertions alongside the deep-equal.

## Deliverables

- Golden fixture plus parity test running in the unit profile.
- A doc comment in the test recording what it pins, which adapters it uses, and when the baseline was captured.

## Dependencies

None — safe to land first.

## Provenance

Child of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI. Enforces parent AC1 ("All shipped content
compiles to exactly the same option lists as before") and de-risks AC3/AC5.
data.title: Options-parity golden snapshot for shipped story-line content

# `engine-sync.sync --soft`: an interactive dev-start mode that never blocks on a dirty `./core`

## Problem statement

`scripts/engine-sync.mjs` exposes one sync mode whose first act is a hard guard:

```js
if (submoduleIsDirty(repoRoot, coreRel)) {
  throw new EngineSyncError(`engine:sync: ${coreRel} has uncommitted changes — refusing to sync (never clobber). …`);
}
```

That is correct for build paths (`npm run build`, `build:electron`, `implement.py finish`, the dev-push gate) where a dirty submodule must fail loudly. It makes the same function unusable for an **interactive dev start**: a game repo wants `npm run dev` to compose the current engine `dev` tip, but `./core` is routinely dirty while someone works engine-side, so a strict sync would refuse to start the server exactly when the developer needs it.

Operator decision (this session, Q1) is **option B**: add a soft mode rather than wiring the strict `engine:sync` into `dev`.

## Users / user stories

- **Game developer (downstream `tce-<game>` repo):** "As a game developer, `npm run dev` composes the current engine `dev` tip and starts serving, without me running a build or doing submodule surgery first."
- **Engine developer (dirty `./core`):** "As a developer with uncommitted engine edits, `npm run dev` still starts on my working tree, with a loud warning that the engine sync was skipped — my changes are never clobbered or blocked."
- **Release operator (unchanged):** "As a release operator, nothing about `engine:verify` or the strict `engine:sync` build path changes; a dirty submodule still fails a release/build loudly."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `syncEngine({ …, soft: true })` and the CLI `node scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft` exist. With a **dirty** `./core` they perform **no git operation**, log a loud, actionable warning naming the submodule and the reason, and return/exit `0` with `{ updated: false, … , skipped: 'dirty' }` (or equivalent documented field) instead of throwing.
2. Strict mode is **byte-for-byte unchanged**: `sync` without `--soft` (and `syncEngine()` with no `soft` key) still throws the existing `EngineSyncError` message on a dirty submodule, so `npm run build` / `build:electron` / the finish gate keep their current failure semantics (regression-tested).
3. Soft mode changes **only** the dirty-guard outcome. Every other path is identical to strict sync: clean + remote ahead → `git submodule update --remote`, loud `from → to` log, pin rewrite when the repo is pinned, return `updated`; offline/unreachable remote → warn and keep the checkout (already soft); clean + already at tip → no pin write. A dirty-submodule soft run must **not** rewrite the pin or stage the gitlink.
4. `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (`renderPackageJson`) emits the two scripts that let a game repo use soft mode:
   - `dev: "npm run engine:dev-sync && vite --host"`
   - `engine:dev-sync: "node <coreRel>/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft"`
   and the rendered `package.json` for `main-street` matches the committed `tce-main-street/package.json` for those two entries.
5. `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` types are updated (`soft?: boolean` on the sync options, the new result field, `SyncResult` doc comment) and `tsc --noEmit` passes for consumers of the declarations.
6. Engine-side tests in `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` cover: (a) dirty submodule + `soft: true` → resolves, no throw, no update, no pin write, warning reported; (b) dirty submodule + strict → still throws the existing message; (c) clean submodule + `soft: true` → same result as strict (update + pin rewrite + staging); (d) CLI `sync --soft` exit code `0` with the warning on stdout/stderr and `sync` exit code `1` on the same fixture; (e) scaffold render assertion for the two scripts (extend the existing render test).
7. CLI usage text documents `--soft` and its dev-start intent; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (engine) describes the two modes (strict = build/release gate, soft = interactive dev start) wherever `engine:sync` is documented, and the canonical script header comment is updated.
8. All related documentation is updated (engine `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, script docblocks, npm-script comments in the scaffold template).
9. Full project test suite passes; `npm run build` (strict TypeScript + Vite) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo ordering:** the engine commit lands on engine `dev` **first**; the downstream gitlink bump + `configs/engine-pin.json` re-pin is tracked in the paired `tce-main-street` item — do not bump from here.
- **No new failure semantics for gates.** Soft mode must be opt-in per call site; no build/release script may use it.
- **Never clobber.** Soft mode's dirty outcome is "skip and warn", never "stash/reset/checkout over" the developer's edits.
- **Scaffold ownership:** the `dev` / `engine:dev-sync` scripts belong in `renderPackageJson`, never hand-edited into a game repo's `package.json`.
- **Do not disturb the dirty engine checkout** at `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` — its main checkout currently has 3 modified `example-games/gym/content/*` files from unrelated work; work in the implement worktree.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc.
- UK English in all written output.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` — `syncEngine({ soft })`, CLI `--soft` flag parsing + usage text, header docblock describing strict vs soft.
- `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` — `soft?: boolean`, result field, doc comments.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `dev` + `engine:dev-sync` in `renderPackageJson` with an explanatory comment.
- `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` — soft/strict/dirty/clean/CLI cases (fixtures already exist for sync/verify).
- scaffold render test (`grep renderPackageJson` in `tests/scripts/`) — assert the two rendered scripts.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine-sync mode table (strict vs soft) and the "when to use which" rule.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: soft mode masks a stale engine.** Mitigation: the warning is loud and names the reason; strict build paths still catch lag at `engine:verify`/pin. No silent success.
- **Risk: two modes drift.** Mitigation: one code path with a single conditional on the dirty-guard outcome, proven by tests (a) and (c) asserting result equality with strict mode.
- **Risk: game repos start staging pin/gitlink bumps on every `npm run dev`.** Accepted (the pin travels with the gitlink by policy, CG-0MVO268500071BPI) and mitigated by the existing loud `from → to` / pin-log lines; recorded in the paired downstream item.
- **Risk: npm script name proliferation.** Bounded to one wrapper (`engine:dev-sync`) that exists only so `dev` can pass `--soft`; `engine:sync` keeps its meaning.
- **Assumption:** downstream repos invoke the script exactly as scaffolded (`node ./core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft`), so no arguments ever reach `dev` from npm.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — original engine-sync/verify + scaffold wiring (strict sync in `build`, `verify` in `build:release`); this item adds the opt-in soft mode it did not need then.
- **CG-0MVO268500071BPI** — pin-tracks-tip policy: the pin and the `./core` gitlink always travel together.
- **CG-0MVTVSYQE002JGDN** — git hermeticity contract (`REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`) that soft mode must keep honouring.
- **CG-0MVOCF9T5007CH2A** — local-suite coverage of the pin policy and lag-vs-bad-pin diagnostics (pattern for the new tests).
- **CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN** — current in-flight engine item; unrelated, listed to avoid worktree collisions.

## Appendix: decision record

- **Q1 — how should an interactive dev start compose the engine?** Options: (A) strict `npm run engine:sync && vite --host` (dev fails loudly on a dirty submodule); (B) opt-in soft sync mode used by `dev`, strict paths untouched; (C) hand-edit only the game repo's `package.json` (clobbered by re-scaffold). **Answer (operator, this session): B.** Source: producer chat — "Make run dev also run engine:sync" → presented options A/B/C with consequences → "B".
data.title: engine-sync: add a --soft sync mode for interactive dev starts (never block on a dirty ./core)
